content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`; read `AGENTS.md` first. The shell harness (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, built as target `shell_integration_harness`, run as `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --<mode>`) drives the real app through about forty automated modes. On 2026-11-16 another session ran every automated mode on commit `b3eed3bf4b` (an ancestor of `jusprin-dev`) and found five modes whose checks fail there. These failures predate that session's work and nobody has looked for their causes. `jusprin-dev` has moved seven commits since, including `f88b40865c` (printer chat connects every print host type), so the list may have changed. Constraints: build with `-- -j4`, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building, one build per build directory; see the memory note on building in a worktree (reuse `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64`, `BUILD_TESTS=ON`). Never apply a fix for a failure you have not reproduced. Do not drive Kenneth's own running JusPrin; the harness uses its own data directory. Commit on your own branch only; do not push and do not touch `jusprin-dev`. Another branch, `claude/bold-mestorf-858777`, changes error handling and the harness and is not landed; do not build on it and expect to rebase if it lands first.

Task:
Find out why these shell-harness modes fail on `jusprin-dev`, and fix each one.

Failures seen on `b3eed3bf4b` (re-run each on the current `jusprin-dev` head first and record what fails now):
- `--print-issues`: 6 checks about a reply that is still running, for example `buttons_are_disabled_while_a_reply_is_running`.
- `--print-issue-readers`: 8 checks, for example `a4_toolpath_outside_in_orcas_words` (wording or profile differences from OrcaSlicer).
- `--printer-network-check`: `first_read_tool_called`.
- `--printer-connect-skill`: 3 checks, for example `connect_skill_printer_added`.
- `--project-prompt-requests`: `print-hook-plan-slice_answer_printer_list_has_its_result`; one to three more checks vary with machine load.
- `--printer-chat-sheet` crashed on exit (exit 139) twice while the machine was heavily loaded and never again in 13 quiet runs; note it only if you see it.

For each failing check decide which is wrong, the app or the check. Use `git log -S` / `git blame` to find the commit that changed the behaviour or the check, and say which. If the app is wrong, fix the app and show the check failing before and passing after. If the check is stale, update it to what the app is meant to do and name the commit that made it stale. If a failure depends on timing or load, say so with the evidence (how many runs, how many failures) and fix the wait rather than raising a timeout blindly.

Done looks like: each of the five modes exits 0 on your branch, one commit per cause with the reason in the message, the agent tests (`build/arm64/tests/agent/Release/agent_bridge_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/agent_bridge_tests`) still pass, and a final report with one line per check: what was wrong, the commit that caused it, and what you changed. List anything you could not reproduce and left alone.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a

metadata:

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

commit 5e173c5e15c2c6744b00529442077a268b367284
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 12 20:48:21 2026 -0800

    Fix the shell harness runs that 6b59a887ca and the 2.5.0 merge broke
    
    Commit 6b59a887ca fails a chat's turn when the chat's provider has no
    stored key. The recorder, reply-choices and calibration runs use a mock
    model with no key, so they hung on their second message, as the default
    run did before 084b8d35a7. Those runs now store the placeholder key too.
    
    Running every chat mode then showed other failures, not caused by that
    commit, now fixed:
    
    - A calibration made from a person's project lost its project and chat.
      OrcaSlicer's generator moves the project folder twice, and the flag
      that keeps the project going was used up by the first move. It now
      holds for the whole generation (ProjectPersistence).
    - A calibration test reopened from Home did not say "Opened from Home".
      Opening replaces the document more than once, and the first
      replacement used up the mark. The mark now names the project id and is
      used only by that project's document.
    - Autosave saved a project again after an idle wait. OrcaSlicer's
      project info panel creates an empty info record when it refreshes,
      and autosave counted that as a change. It now compares the record's
      contents, so no record and an empty one are the same.
    - The calibration and setup-differences mocks sent one value for
      settings that hold one per nozzle type since the 2.5.0 merge
      (nozzle_temperature, initial_layer_speed); they send two now.
    - Three checks expected stale text: Home says "Draft" for a project
      never printed, and the All settings panel heads a printer setting with
      its page and group ("Extruder · Retraction").
    - The recorder now keeps a "busy" answer to a slice read made while the
      turn's own slice runs, which is what the app tells the model there.
      The README says how long recording takes and how those three points
      depend on timing.
    
    The harness prints a failed tool's error code and message, not only its
    empty result.
    
    Tested on macOS: every chat mode of shell_integration_harness passes
    (default, chat-restoration, file-opening, task-chat, account-box,
    printer-chat-sheet, check-print, mcp, reply-choices, setup-differences,
    timeline, calibration, tool-strip and reopen-prompt captures),
    --autosave-seed and --autosave-reopen pass, and agent_bridge_tests
    passes (577 cases). The workspace harness fails 2 checks
    (second_model_dropped, model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit), down from
    11; those 2 failed before this change too. The recorder
    (--project-prompt-requests) still fails 3 checks at the three points
    where the turn's slice is running, because that slice can end partway
    through the reads; requests.json is not recorded again here.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M79KREEGB3QHM0Q7M2NXKY2Y

    Shell harness: the default run's mock AI has a key, as a person's would
    
    Since 6b59a887ca the app keeps a chat the person has talked in on its
    provider, and fails the next turn with "This chat ran on OpenAI, and no
    OpenAI API key is set up now" when no key for it is stored. The harness's
    default run installed its mock AI with the AI turned off and no key, a
    state the app itself never reaches, so the chat's second message ("please
    duplicate the selected object") failed that way and the run waited
    forever for the tool to succeed.
    
    The default run now stores a placeholder OpenAI key with the AI turned on,
    as the configured task-chat capture already does, and points OpenAI at a
    closed local port so the key never leaves the machine.
    
    Tested: the default run passes, 631 checks with no failures; before, it
    hung after 281. A temporary print showed the failing turn's error was
    chat_provider_removed.

The chip's button sends "Explain this issue and my options.": a question, so answer it and leave the project as it is. When the person then asks you to fix it, change what the issue names, and only that; anything else worth changing is a suggestion.

How to read a finding. A blocker means I will not slice or print until it is fixed; a warning means the slice exists and can print; a critical warning is one I flag as serious. The setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now. The object, when named, narrows where; with none it is about the plate or the setup. count says how many warnings there are; read slice_report's findings when more than the first matters. An ignored one is a finding the person chose not to be told about again: still true of the slice. Explain a finding from its words, never from a cause you supply.

A warning is my statement about the slice, not proof the print will fail. Say what it risks for this print and its purpose. # JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where
the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails
while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder.

The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like
`<0>…</0>` for elements inside a `Trans`, and
`{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the
placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a
plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses
(`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`).

## Marking text

Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items,
tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error
text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly
as it was.

Leave these in English, unmarked:

- **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool
  results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a
  request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and
  `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the
  person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown.
- Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes,
  test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code.
- Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`,
  `report_error`): they are read by developers.
- Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names.
